text:
Sofia: Noticed a spike in onboarding questions about require/import and some flaky behavior in our sample app when run in Edge vs node. Filed an internal issue but thought I'd check here for quick ideas.

Alex: Can you share the exact error? Edge usually complains 'require is not defined' or bundlers produce module parse errors.

Sofia: Error from a user running the sample: `ReferenceError: require is not defined` when deployed to Vercel Edge. Locally using node 18 the sample worked with `require` because their dev bundler converted it, but Edge failed.

Ramesh: Classic. Our SDK publishes both ESM and CJS entries, but some bundlers pick the wrong one depending on package.json "exports" and environment. We probably need clearer guidance: for Next.js Edge API routes you must use native ESM imports or the Edge build will fail.

Sofia: Proposed docs text: short explanation + 3 in-repo snippets: ESM Edge, Node CJS, TypeScript tsconfig.

Alex: Add a note about named vs default: we export `default` as the main client class but also have some named helpers. That confuses folks doing `const { Redwood } = require('@redwood/inference')` which returns undefined. Suggest examples for both patterns.

Ramesh: Also mention `esModuleInterop` in TS. People running into `Cannot use import statement outside a module` sometimes have wrong module setting. Offer minimal tsconfig.

docs-bot: draft PR created for docs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/484

Sofia: Cool. Can we also mention this in the sample-app README and add a note in the Next.js template about `export const config = { runtime: 'edge' }` requiring ESM?

CI-bot: CI passed for docs PR 484.

Sofia: Great. I'll follow up with a quick changelog blurb. Thanks :heart:
